technical_and_design_decisions: Each migrated module will be re-implemented as a standalone Spring Cloud Stream application (app starter) packaged as an executable Spring Boot fat jar, rather than a copy of the original Spring XD module.

Sources (syslog, mail, tcp, tcp-client) will be built on the Spring Cloud Stream source model using @EnableBinding(Source.class) (or the functional equivalent), and sinks (gpfdist, hdfs-dataset, mail, mongo) on @EnableBinding(Sink.class).
Module options from Spring XD will be refactored into typed @ConfigurationProperties classes with Spring Boot configuration metadata so that options are exposed as application properties.
Spring Boot auto-configuration will be used to wire each module's beans, keeping the modules usable both as standalone apps and as libraries in composed pipelines.

Existing Spring Integration-based logic from the Spring XD modules (e.g., TCP channel adapters and codecs/deserializers, mail inbound adapters, JavaMailSender for outbound mail, MongoDB outbound adapters) will be reused and adapted instead of rewritten from scratch.
Target baseline is Java 17+ consistent with Spring Framework 6.x / current Spring Cloud Stream generation stated in the specification.

Each module gets unit tests plus integration tests (e.g., embedded/test servers for TCP and syslog, GreenMail-style fake SMTP for mail, embedded MongoDB for mongo, and containerized/stubbed HDFS and Greenplum/gpfdist endpoints for the data sinks) using the Spring Cloud Stream test binder.
Each module ships with Asciidoc reference documentation describing its properties and usage as a source or sink.
Maven multi-module build under a common parent POM (Spring Cloud Stream app starters conventions), with CI pipeline configuration for the new modules.

The mail module appears in two user stories (U2 as source, U7 as sink); these will be delivered as two separate apps (mail-source and mail-sink) that share mail connection property conventions, with the second migration benefiting from the first.
assumptions: The existing Spring XD module source code for all eight modules is available, stable, and functionally correct; the goal is behavior-parity migration, not feature enhancement.
The developer performing the work is experienced with Spring XD internals, Spring Integration, Spring Boot, and the Spring Cloud Stream programming model.
Target Spring Cloud Stream repository structure, naming conventions, and contribution guidelines already exist; only module-level work plus minor build/CI wiring is required.

Test infrastructure (fake/embedded SMTP server, embedded MongoDB, containerized or stubbed HDFS and Greenplum/gpfdist endpoints) is available or can be embedded in the build without additional environment provisioning effort.

Effort per module includes: analysis of the original XD module, app skeleton creation, porting of core logic, configuration properties and auto-configuration, unit and integration tests, per-module documentation, and code-review/rework iterations.
Effort excludes: writing new end-user features beyond parity, performance/load testing, security audits, and publishing/releasing artifacts to public repositories beyond standard release preparation.
No clarifying questions are needed; any gaps in the specification (module behavior details, binder targets, build system) are covered by the technical and design decisions above.
Estimates are pure development effort (work-hours) for a single developer, not elapsed calendar time.

activities.activity_description: Analyze the eight Spring XD modules, map their options to typed properties, define the shared migration approach (auto-configuration pattern, binder usage, testing strategy), and produce a per-module migration plan and checklist.
Set up the Maven multi-module structure under the app-starters parent POM, module archetype/skeleton generation, dependency management, and CI pipeline configuration for the new modules.

Port the XD syslog module to a Spring Cloud Stream source: syslog server listener (TCP/UDP) wiring, message parsing, typed configuration properties, auto-configuration, unit and integration tests with a test listener, and Asciidoc documentation.

Port the XD mail module to a Spring Cloud Stream source: IMAP/POP3 inbound mail integration (Spring Integration mail adapters), message transformation, typed configuration properties, auto-configuration, integration tests against a fake mail server, and documentation.

Port the XD tcp module to a Spring Cloud Stream source: TCP server socket factory, decoders/serializers and message framing options, typed configuration properties, auto-configuration, integration tests over real sockets, and documentation.

Port the XD tcp-client module to a Spring Cloud Stream source: outbound client connection with retry/reconnect handling, decoder configuration, typed properties (reusing TCP codec conventions from U3), auto-configuration, integration tests, and documentation.

Port the XD gpfdist module to a Spring Cloud Stream sink: gpfdist protocol handling and data staging for Greenplum loading, load orchestration and error handling, typed configuration properties, auto-configuration, integration tests against stubbed/containerized Greenplum and gpfdist endpoints, and documentation.

Port the XD hdfs-dataset module to a Spring Cloud Stream sink: HDFS connectivity, dataset writing (formats, partitioning, naming/rollover options), typed configuration properties, auto-configuration, integration tests against embedded/stubbed HDFS, and documentation.

Implement the mail sink app (SMTP sending via JavaMailSender): typed configuration properties aligned with the mail-source conventions, auto-configuration, integration tests against a fake SMTP server, and documentation. Benefits from prior mail source migration.

Port the XD mongo module to a Spring Cloud Stream sink: MongoDB outbound write path with JSON/field mapping options, typed configuration properties, auto-configuration, integration tests with embedded MongoDB, and documentation.

activities.activity_name: Cross-module integration testing, QA, and release preparation
activities.activity_description: Run end-to-end stream pipeline tests combining the migrated sources and sinks with a test binder, fix cross-cutting defects, verify build reproducibility and documentation completeness, and prepare the increment for release (versioning, release notes).
